//: Copy-paste detection — the duplication half of the QM-4 quality gate (ADR-011).
QM-4 originally read '0% duplication on new code', inherited from SonarQube's quality-gate
vocabulary. Two things make that unenforceable here: jscpd has no concept of 'new code' (it
scans whole files, not a diff), and the repository's measured duplication on 2026-07-21 was
2.80% of lines / 2.95% of tokens across 454 code files — so a 0% gate would fail on the commit
that introduced it.
The threshold below is therefore a RATCHET, not an aspiration: it blocks duplication from
growing past today's level. Lower it as clones are removed.
Measured baseline 2026-07-21, after ADR-021 (min-lines 10, min-tokens 70, tests excluded,
same path list CI passes):
go           0.00%  <- was 23.01%. The two workers' copied internal/coskafka and internal/otel
are now packages of one shared module, libs/go.
tsx          1.33%  <- was 2.18%. Two routes rendered the same budget grid; that body is now
components/finance/FinanceSummaryPanel.tsx. What remains is table and
filter scaffolding repeated across list pages.
typescript   1.20%  <- was 1.50%. Seven repositories under modules/project/ each carried their
own cursor codec; now shared/pagination/cursor.ts. Still the largest
remaining block: NestJS controller/service boilerplate across modules.
python       0.64%  <- untouched, one clone
TOTAL        1.12%  <- was 2.80%
apps/mobile/src ADDED TO THE SCANNED PATHS 2026-08-19. It had never been measured — the largest
tsx tree in the repo (144 files, 38k lines) was outside the only gate that looks for copy-paste,
so a clone there was invisible by construction. Re-measured with it included, same settings:
python       1.07%  <- unchanged, one clone
tsx          1.71%  <- was 1.81% over apps/web alone; mobile is close to the same rate
typescript   0.82%
TOTAL        1.19%  <- was 1.07% without mobile; still inside the 1.5 ratchet
What mobile's own 34 clones were, measured the same day: 29 of them were StyleSheet blocks in
the pinned-dark auth and success screens.
RE-MEASURED 2026-08-20, after that cluster was worked. The first reading above ('only 9 keys are
byte-identical') compared the screens PAIRWISE and understated it: comparing all 14 files at once
found 16 keys whose value is identical in three or more of them — 71 copies of a style object,
for 16 distinct values. Those 16 are now `darkScreen` in src/theme/screenStyles.ts and the
screens reference it. Nothing was normalised into agreement to get there: a key was extracted
only where the file's own value already matched byte-for-byte, so the keys that decide a given
screen's look and genuinely differ (each screen's `hero`, `card`, `body`, chips, its own
`content` padding) stayed local and no screen's appearance changed.
The two sync indicators' shared ternary went the same day: <SyncPill /> and <OverlaySyncPill />
stay separate components (PO 2026-08-04/09 — the top-bar one is glyph-only, the overlay one is
labelled), but the four states and their precedence are now src/hooks/useSyncPillView.ts. The
copies had already drifted on the SYNCED glyph; that disagreement is a parameter of the hook now
rather than something this refactor picked a winner for.
TOTAL        0.92%  <- was 1.19%
mobile        22 clone pairs  <- was 34
What remains in mobile is not style blocks but JSX bodies — the header/scroll/footer scaffold of
the consent screens, and list screens that draw the same card. Those are components waiting to be
extracted rather than values waiting to be shared, and each needs its own reading.
